department: Faculty of Science — Department of Chemistry

deadline.value: August intake application window runs from May 16 to November 15 of the previous year (January intake closes May 15 of the previous year).
deadline.quote: For August intake: 16 May to 15 November (of the previous year)

gre_subject.value: No ETS GRE Subject Test exists for chemistry (ETS discontinued the Chemistry Subject Test in May 2023).
gre_subject.quote: The GRE Subject Tests in Mathematics, Physics and Psychology measure undergraduate achievement in a particular field of study

supervisor.value: Applicants choose up to 3 proposed PhD supervisors from the Chemistry Faculty / Jointly Appointed Faculty list (and contact proposed supervisors for grant-funded scholarships).
supervisor.quote: Please choose up to 3 proposed PhD supervisors from the “Faculty” and “Jointly Appointed Faculty” sections only

also.quote: PhD Scholarship under research grant (contact the proposed supervisor)

funding.value: Competitive scholarships include NUS Research Scholarship, President's Graduate Fellowship, and the Faculty of Science Dean Graduate Fellowship (top 20% of scholarship holders, adding S$600/month to stipends of S$2,800/month for international students).
funding.quote: PhD Scholarships in Department of Chemistry | NUS Research Scholarship | President’s Graduate Fellowship (PGF) | Dean Graduate Fellowship (DGF) | Selected from those with RSB, SINGA, IRP in admission per AY (top 20%) | Stipends in years 1-4, increase by 600 S$ per month | SC: S$3,400 +CPF 578; SPR: S$3,000; IS: S$2,800

entry_route.value: Requires a 4-year bachelor's or Honours degree (at least 2nd Class Upper Honours or equivalent for Research Scholarship applicants).
entry_route.quote: A Bachelor’s (Honours) degree or a 4-year Bachelor’s degree | Candidates applying for Research Scholarships must have obtained a bachelor’s degree with at least a 2nd Class Upper Honours, or its equivalent.

gre_general.value: Chemistry strongly encourages all PhD candidates to submit GRE scores (minimum 320 Verbal + Quantitative and 3.5 Analytical Writing).
gre_general.quote: For all PhD programmes, candidates are strongly encouraged to submit GRE (minimum score of 320 [Verbal+ Quantitative] and 3.5 [Analytical Writing]).

toefl_min.value: Chemistry requires TOEFL iBT 5 on the new scale (95 on the old scale) or IELTS 7.0 if undergraduate instruction was not in English.
toefl_min.quote: a candidate whose medium of undergraduate instruction is not English is required to submit TOEFL (with the minimum score 95 (old scale) or 5 (new scale) for the internet-based test) or IELTS (with the minimum score 7.0) scores.

ielts_min.value: Chemistry requires IELTS 7.0 overall (or TOEFL iBT 95 old / 5 new scale) if undergraduate instruction was not in English.
ielts_min.quote: a candidate whose medium of undergraduate instruction is not English is required to submit TOEFL (with the minimum score 95 (old scale) or 5 (new scale) for the internet-based test) or IELTS (with the minimum score 7.0) scores.

notes: Department-specific higher English thresholds (TOEFL 95 old / 5 new, IELTS 7.0) and GRE recommendation override NUS baseline.
